entries.title: Amazon Big Deal Deals Starts October 6th
entries.summary: Amazon has announced some early deals for the Big Deals Page; the event will kick off on October 6th. The post Amazon Big Deal Deals Starts October 6th first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days 2026 is shaping up to be a highly strategic, 48-hour shopping event scheduled for Tuesday, October 6, through Wednesday, October 7, 2026. Functioning as the true kickoff to the Q4 holiday shopping momentum, early reviews from major consumer outlets note that while the summer Prime Day event remains larger, this October iteration serves as a powerful preview for Black Friday pricing, particularly on small appliances, robot vacuums, and Amazon hardware

Curl up this fall with great reads—get three months free of Kindle Unlimited to dive into trending series like Dungeon Crawler Carl by Matt Dinniman and The Empyrean by Rebecca Yarros—ahead of the highly anticipated next installment. Find thousands of print book deals up to 65% off, including cookbooks perfect for seasonal hosting like Wishbone Kitchen by Meredith Hayden. Plus, Prime members can enjoy one free Amazon First Reads Kindle book and a bonus short read and four months of Audible Standard for $0.99/month. 

  • Kindle Unlimited: 3 months free for new subscribers. As usual, previous subscribers may not be eligible.
  • Audible Standard: $0.99/month for 4 months (Prime members)
  • Amazon First Reads: two free Kindle books for Prime members
  • Print books: up to 65% off on thousands of titles

Amazon will likely put a number of e-readers and e-notebooks on sale, but the biggest deals will occur on Black Friday. It remains to be seen what type of deals will be available, but the company normally heavily discounts the bundles, which include a case, charger and other goodies.

entries.title: XTEINK S4 is available now with USB-C and a front-light
entries.summary: The XTEINK S4 is highly praised by reviewers as the ultimate pocket e-reader for its ultra-compact, MagSafe-compatible design, an open Android 11 OS that supports popular reading apps, and the much-needed addition of an adjustable front light. The post XTEINK S4 is available now with USB-C and a front-light first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The XTEINK S4 is an upcoming 4.3-inch pocket e-ink e-reader from Chinese tech startup Xteink. Serving as the highly anticipated successor to the ultra-thin XTEINK X4, the S4 shifts from a proprietary Linux-based OS to an open Android 11 platform. This change allows readers to natively sideload Android APKs like Kindle, Kobo, and KOReader.

The XTEINK S4 is a pocket-sized e-reader with a 4.3-inch E-ink touchscreen at 220 PPI, built into a compact frame that weighs just 95 grams and measures 6.98 mm thick. Abandoning its predecessor’s restrictive custom firmware, the device runs on an open 32-bit Android 11 operating system, giving users the flexibility to sideload major reading apps like Kindle, Kobo, and KOReader. The hardware layout retains the brand’s signature physical side page-turn buttons alongside a single front home button, and it incorporates built-in magnets on the backplate to snap seamlessly onto MagSafe-compatible phone cases.

Internally, the device runs on 2GB of RAM and 32GB of built-in storage for local digital libraries. To address previous layout limitations, it includes an integrated, temperature-adjustable cool and warm front light for reading in the dark, along with a vastly expanded 1,400mAh battery. Connectivity includes built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for wireless book transfers or audio listening, plus a primary USB-C port for charging and data syncing.

This device is currently only available in China, but the company will likely release it internationally in the coming months.

entries.title: Amazon brought influences to Lab126
entries.summary: Amazon invited a number of young book influencers to tour their secretive RND LAB126 in California. The post Amazon brought influences to Lab126 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon Lab126 is Amazon’s research, development, and hardware engineering subsidiary located in Sunnyvale, California, within the San Francisco Bay Area. Researchers developed the Kindle, Fire tablets, and Fire TV products there. They continue to develop the next generation products here, such as the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft.

A couple of days ago, Amazon invited a bunch of young influencers to tour the facility. This included Lottie Smalley, Khalilah D, and Kendall Ferrari. They spoke with several executives and researchers at the facility to learn about industrial design and product development.

Amazon has plans to release a number of new  e-readers this year. They will likely incorporate a faster processor and more RAM in order to take advantage of AI features that are more advanced than Kindle Recaps and Story So Far. One of the big changes will be user-replaceable batteries that use common screws on the back panel for easy removal, and not using glue to hold the battery in place. They are primarily refreshing the Kindle lineup to remain in coplience to a new EU battery law taking effect in early 2027.

entries.title: Amazon changes all images for Kindle books to AVIF
entries.summary: The main Amazon website now serves Kindle Book and Kindle E-Reader images as AVIF, not PNG or JPEG. The post Amazon changes all images for Kindle books to AVIF first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon has changed some product images on its website across all properties from PNG or JPEG to .avif. This also affects Kindle Book cover art and Kindle e-reader images. The only way to download the files in the old format is to open a private browser and download them, but it remains to be seen how long this will work.

AVIF (AV1 Image File Format) is a modern, open-source, and royalty-free image file format used to store still and animated images with much smaller file sizes than traditional formats like JPEG or PNG. The Alliance for Open Media (a group including tech giants like Google, Netflix, Amazon, and Microsoft) developed it and first released it in 2019. The format improves site loading speeds, which is why Amazon is slowly adopting it.

One downside of the new image format is that users can no longer simply download the files and post them on their own websites, since most CMSs, such as WordPress, do not natively support it. Calibre, a popular e-book management program, also doesn’t support the format, so users must source cover art from Open Library instead of Amazon.

These e-book and product image issues occur only on the main Amazon website and some international versions; Amazon Canada still serves them with JPEG and PNG.

entries.title: E INK invests in NewCopper for copper ink tech
entries.summary: E Ink Announces Strategic Investment in NewCopper to Advance Conductive Copper Ink Technology. The post E INK invests in NewCopper for copper ink tech first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E INK has just made a significant investment in NewCopper, a privately held U.S. technology startup developing conductive copper ink. NewCopper’s technology originated from breakthrough joint research by the University of Maryland and Yale University. NewCopper holds an exclusive license from the University of Maryland for the proprietary copper ink formulation.

As flexible electronics expand into applications such as displays, sensors, solar technology, RFID and connected devices, manufacturers are seeking alternatives to high-cost silver ink, which is widely used to create conductive pathways in printed components. Copper offers strong conductivity at a lower material cost, but its susceptibility to oxidation has historically limited its broader adoption. NewCopper developed a proprietary low-temperature, reactive and self-passivating copper ink formulation designed to overcome this challenge.

E Ink will make the investment through a post-money Simple Agreement for Future Equity (SAFE) and leverage its display manufacturing expertise to support NewCopper’s production scale-up and commercialization. Because NewCopper’s formulation is compatible with E Ink’s roll-to-roll coating capabilities, the investment also gives E Ink’s R&D team an opportunity to evaluate copper ink as a potential conductive material for future displays and electrode applications. More broadly, the collaboration strengthens the localized supply chain for advanced electronic materials and supports the future production of ePaper components.

“E Ink itself spun out of academia into a global technology company, so we recognize both the promise of NewCopper’s innovation and the challenges of moving breakthrough technology from the lab to the market,” said Johnson Lee, chairman and CEO of E Ink. “As an established leader in materials and display manufacturing, it’s our responsibility to help promising companies scale. By supporting NewCopper with resources, expertise and commercialization experience, we can also help guide the display industry to new heights.”

entries.title: Kindle Scribe Premium Pen on sale for 40% off
entries.summary: The Kindle Scribe Premium Pen is available in tungsten or metallic jade, and both colors are currently discounted to the same price. The post Kindle Scribe Premium Pen on sale for 40% off first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Kindle Scribe Premium Pen is on sale for $47.99 on Amazon, a 40% discount off the list price. It is also on sale on the Amazon Canada site and the UK site.

The Kindle Scribe Pen features a dedicated top-mounted digital eraser, a customizable shortcut button for quick tool swapping, and magnetic attachment capabilities. It operates on battery-free EMR technology, so it never needs to charge. Plus, the pen can do more than take notes. You can underline and highlight text in books, as well as use it for lists, journals, and other handwritten notes.

Amazon Kindle Scribe Premium Pen, Sleek Stylus Design with Improved Eraser - Tungsten

  • Designed exclusively for your Kindle Scribe - Sleek design, color matches with your device and improved eraser so you can write as naturally as you do on paper (compatible with Kindle Scribe—will not work on any other Kindle).
  • Unlocks digital note-taking - Write, underline, and highlight directly in books, create journals and lists, and more—all with high precision.
  • Start writing instantly - No setup or pairing required to start writing, and battery-free, so no need to worry about charging.

Buying a new e-reader is highly compelling because the hardware market has shifted from minor iterative updates to radical, quality-of-life transformations. If your current e-reader is more than three or four years old, you are missing out on significant upgrades in display tech, ecosystem independence, and everyday responsiveness.

The XTEINK X4 Classic (also known as the X4 V2) is an ultra-thin, pocket-sized E-Ink eReader designed to snap onto the back of a smartphone or slip effortlessly into a pocket. Released in September 2026, it serves as the direct successor to the original X4 (which has been discontinued) and refines the “pure” tiny reader concept by prioritizing physical controls and extreme portability over touchscreens

  • Dual Page-Turn & Flexible Book Transfer: Choose physical buttons or shake-to-turn for convenient one-handed reading. Easily transfer and convert books or comics via XTEINK App transfer, microSD Card or USB, with support for TXT, EPUB, MOBI, PDF and PNG formats. Data is processed locally.

entries.title: eBooks.com has launched two new reading apps for iOS and Android
entries.summary: The new reading apps are now available for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. They seamlessly support a wide range of ebook formats, including fixed-format EPUB, audio-visual content, manga, and textbooks with complex layouts and specialized fonts. The post eBooks.com has launched two new reading apps for iOS and Android first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
eBooks.com has launched completely new iOS and Android reading apps, developed through an Australian-European partnership. The launch forms part of a wider renewal of our reading platform, including Readium LCP, our new Online Reader, and support for Thorium.

The new reading apps are now available for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. They seamlessly support a wide range of ebook formats, including fixed-format EPUB, audio-visual content, manga, and textbooks with complex layouts and specialized fonts.

Developed in partnership with the European Digital Reading Lab and Sweden’s Colibrio, the new apps provide a simpler, faster, and more accessible reading experience, with support for offline reading, extensive typography and display controls, and modern accessibility features.

The apps form part of eBooks.com’s transition to open, standards-based reading technologies, including Readium LCP. They follow the company’s recent introduction of a new browser-based Online Reader and its support for the Thorium desktop reading application.

eBooks.com’s founder, Stephen Cole, said, “Our new reading platform is a delight to use. It’s bristling with useful features and is built with a clear focus on accessibility, simplicity and interoperability. It will support eBooks.com’s continued growth for years to come.

“I am especially proud of the apps’ attention to the needs of readers with disabilities. The new apps integrate with the assistive technologies built into iOS and Android, including VoiceOver and TalkBack. But they also provide extensive additional controls over typography and presentation. Readers can alter text size, typeface, spacing, alignment, colours, margins and other aspects of the page. We have also developed reading options intended to make ebooks more comfortable for people with dyslexia and other reading or visual preferences.”

entries.title: XTEINK says they will include USB-C ports on future devices
entries.summary: XTEINK has disclosed that future e-book readers will continue to use both pogo pins and USB-C for charging. The post XTEINK says they will include USB-C ports on future devices first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
The Xteink X4 Classic, X4 Pro, and X3 use pogo pins to charge. The company chose this charging method to keep its devices as thin and light as possible. However, there has been some serious backlash, since the popular X4 model had a USB-C port, which made charging super easy and put Xteink on the map.

Xteink currently offers no models with USB-C ports, and the anti-pogo complaints are becoming too loud to ignore. The company took to Reddit to solicit consumer feedback. They stated, “X4 Classic is a product where we wanted to keep pushing the physical form of the original X4: lighter, thinner, and closer to something that simply disappears into the things you already carry. For X4 Classic, we prioritized the device’s physical form over the convenience of a universal port.”

They went on to say, ” There are people who want the smallest, lightest reading device possible. And there are people who would happily accept a slightly thicker device in exchange for USB-C, a front light, touch, or other conveniences. We’ll keep exploring thinner and lighter e-Readers, while also working toward bringing USB-C back as an option in future products. That work has already started.”

It seems Xteink will focus on a few key areas. A feature-rich e-reader with a front light, touchscreen, a cheaper model, and a future device with a USB-C port to appeal to a wide array of users. Xteink has to listen to its users because they are a small company and has to cater to its fans. They certainly aren’t Amazon, where they can do whatever they want, and people will still buy them.

entries.title: Kobo fixes the e-book syncing problem
entries.summary: Rakuten Kobo has rebuilt its e-reader and app syncing system for bookmarks and e-book progress. Here is how you can fix it on your devices. The post Kobo fixes the e-book syncing problem first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
In Kobo’s early days, they knew most people would buy one of their e-readers, buy books on them, and read. As the company matured, they released a series of new devices virtually every year and maintained a whole suite of mobile apps and a cloud reader. The syncing system was bursting at the seams, and new books and reading progress weren’t working properly.

Kobo CEO Michael Tambyn took to Bluesky to outline what they have done to solve the syncing issue. “We know some of you have been driven slowly crazy by the way your reading progress on the Kobo app doesn’t always correctly sync with your e-reader or your e-reader to your app. Annoying. Bad experience. No one liked it. So we rebuilt the entire bookmarking and progress syncing system from the ground up.”

He went on to say, “First off, this only matters if you are an e-reader and an app user. Or a multi-ereader user. If you aren’t trying to keep two devices in sync, this hasn’t been a problem for you. If you are using an e-reader, go into Settings > Device Information> Repair Your Kobo Account. Or, for apps, sign out of your account and then sign back in. You have to do this on all devices you’re signed in to, but you only have to do it once; after that, everything will stay synced from now on.”
